Clarity.justification: The paper is exceptionally well-written with a logical structure, clear articulation of the specification triple, experimental conditions, and verification protocol. Sections flow coherently from introduction through related work, method, setup, results (verification only), and discussion, with explicit tables and pre-registered predictions.

Novelty.justification: The work presents a structured specification-aligned repair oracle motivated by prior literature (e.g., docstring grounding from Haeri & Ghelichi 2026, contrastive pairs from Kong et al. 2024) but does not introduce fundamentally new ideas. The four-condition verification protocol and pre-registration on EvalPlus semantic failures are incremental contributions rather than groundbreaking advances.

Soundness.justification: The data infrastructure verification (C1-C4 conditions, pytest tests passing in 2.32s, 128-task working set) is rigorously implemented and consistent with the provided code (verify_h_e1_v2.py confirms all gates). However, all comparative claims (P1-P3) remain INCONCLUSIVE with no mechanism experiments executed, limiting full soundness assessment of the core hypothesis.

Significance.justification: The paper addresses semantic failures in LLM code generation (static analysis catches only 16-32.4%), an important problem aligned with the VerifAI workshop theme. Yet as a Stage 1 infrastructure/pre-registration report with no empirical results or impact demonstrated, its contributions to the field are minimal and unlikely to have lasting influence.

strengths: Rigorous pre-experiment verification protocol and code reproducibility
Clear pre-registration of predictions following open science practices
weaknesses: No mechanism experiment results; all key predictions remain INCONCLUSIVE
Incremental novelty with heavy reliance on cited prior work without new empirical validation
